"Residents lodge fresh legal bid to stop Drumcree march"
Protesters remained on the Garvaghy Road overnight; main parties still in stalemate following a day of political talks and heated exchanges at Stormont. Orange Order members waited to begin their permitted parade, due Sunday morning, down the mainly nationalist Garvaghy Road in Portadown.
The two most senior members of Portadown Orange Order met Sir Chris Bryant at Hillsborough Castle; they described the hour-long talks as "constructive".
BREANDAN MAC CIONNAITH, Garvaghy Road Residents Coalition: said the Orange Order should use their outward route to Drumcree Church as their return route, rather than the Garvaghy Road.
SIR CHRIS BRYANT, Northern Ireland Secretary, who returned from the Labour conference for talks: urged both sides to "double down on compromise".
Background: banned since 1998; Parades Commission reversed its determination on Friday 25 September permitting a parade of 35 participants with an 08:00 start instead of the 60 and 13:00 requested; upheld in Belfast courts on Saturday hours before it was due.
